text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Japan's motor manufacturer Isuzu will invest $380 million in the Katowice Special Economic Zone (KSEZ) in southern Poland, the KSEZ president Michal Lichon said.

- The Sanitec Oy Ltd water-closet maker, controlled by Finland's METRA, has acquired part of the Wloclawek-based china factory for 100 million markka and will start its second sanitary porcelain production line in Poland next year.
- Poland's Main Customs Office (GUC) will require up to 778 million zlotys by 2000 for the customs services' modernisation and adapting to the EU regulations.
- The average monthly salary in the first three quarters of 1996 was 862.99 zlotys, showing 25.4 percent growth over the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Stalowa Wola region municipalities will invest two million zlotys in the local Turbia airport's modernisation in 1997, the municipalities said.

- Poland's second biggest Browary Tyskie (BT) brewery has already exceeded its last year's output of 1.581 million hectolitres and plans 1997 annual output of 1.75 million hectolitres. The BT breweries have 11.1 percent of Poland's beer market.
- The French Soprema insulation maker and Danish and Swedish firms have expressed interest in buying stakes in the Nidzica-based Izolacja insulation firm to be listed on the Warsaw bourse next year.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's banking climate index fell by 1.1 point to 51.4 points in November. However, the overall banking climate is still good, Pentor polling institute president Eugeniusz Smilowski said.

- In the second quarter of 1997 Poland's 15 National Investment Funds (NFI) will be listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (WSE), the treasury vice-minister responsible for privatisation Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.
- The PZL Swidnik aviation plant is developing a prototype of the first Polish aircraft to be made of composite materials which will carry four persons and fly up to 1,000 km at 250 km an hour.
- Only 25 percent of Poles think that Poland is a democracy and 33 percent think they live in an undemocratic state, the CBOS polling institute said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's foreign trade deficit in the first nine months of 1996 reached $5.26 billion, the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, said.

- In 1997 the treasury ministry will raise the share capital of the Poznan-based Hipolit Cegielski plant and pass it over to an envisaged holding of Polish shipyards, the treasury vice-minister for privatisation, Wieslaw Kaczmarek, said.
- The RTL 7 television has contracted cartoons produced by the Bielsko-Biala-based animated film studio and will broadcast them for the next two years.
ZYCIE
- Around 40 international firms are participating in the Warsaw professional career fair which will help university graduates and future employers meet their respective needs.

- "We are not against foreign investments; we only want Polish retailers to get the same opportunities as those granted to the great supermarket chains", the Polish retailers' lobbying body (NRZPHU) president Grazyna Tarnas said.
PARKIET
- The annual net profit of the listed Energoaparatura electrical equipment maker will exceed the previous forecasts by five percent, the company said.

- The listed Optimus computer maker will cover the liabilities of its $30 million convertible bond issue in 2.5 years thanks to successful investments in multimedia and Internet, the company president Roman Kluska said.
